label: PASS — PHEP Emergency Preparedness, Accurate Parameters, Strong Compliance Language

generated_draft.background: The Public Health Emergency Preparedness (PHEP) cooperative agreement is the primary federal funding mechanism for building and maintaining state and local public health laboratory emergency readiness. COVID-19 exposed critical gaps in laboratory surge capacity, specimen referral networks, and 24/7 emergency response protocols. This award funds state public health laboratories to achieve and sustain all PHEP laboratory preparedness benchmarks, strengthen All-Hazards surge capacity, and modernize emergency specimen management systems for the post-COVID era. All activities must comply with 2 CFR Part 200 Uniform Guidance and federal grant management requirements.
generated_draft.funding_parameters: Total available funding: $8,500,000. Awards: 20–28. Range per laboratory: $150,000–$600,000. Period of performance: 24 months (July 1, 2021 – June 30, 2023). Federal sponsor: CDC / OPHPR / Division of State and Local Readiness. Cost sharing: not required. Indirect costs allowable up to negotiated rate.
generated_draft.eligibility: Public Health Labs member state or local public health laboratory serving a PHEP-eligible jurisdiction. CLIA high-complexity certification. Current participation in the Laboratory Response Network (LRN-B and LRN-C where applicable). Documented emergency operations plan incorporating laboratory surge protocols. Human subjects research activities funded under this award must comply with 45 CFR Part 46 and applicable state law.
generated_draft.scope_of_work: 1. Achieve all PHEP laboratory capability benchmarks within 18 months: 24/7 testing activation ≤2 hours, inter-laboratory specimen referral protocol documented, mass casualty specimen processing plan for ≥500 specimens/day. 2. Implement or maintain LRN-B threat agent testing proficiency for all Category A agents. 3. Expand electronic laboratory reporting to achieve ≥95% automated ELR for all PHEP-notifiable conditions. 4. Conduct minimum 2 full-scale exercises per year (one tabletop, one functional) with after-action reports within 30 days. 5. Maintain and test emergency stockpile of critical reagents and PPE for 90-day operational continuity.
generated_draft.reporting_requirements: Quarterly PHEP performance measure submissions to CDC DSLR. Exercise after-action reports within 30 days of each exercise. LRN-B proficiency test results per CDC LRN-B protocol. Final report 90 days post-period of performance. All financial reports per 2 CFR Part 200 requirements including SF-425 Federal Financial Report.
generated_draft.budget_requirements: Emergency stockpile reagents and PPE allowable (documented with depletion schedule). Exercise costs (supplies, facilitation, after-action documentation) allowable. ELR interface development costs allowable. 2 CFR Part 200 compliant cost allocation required. No supplanting of existing state funding. Indirect costs at federally negotiated rate only.
generated_draft.evaluation_criteria: Current PHEP benchmark achievement (20 points). Surge capacity plan (25 points). LRN integration and exercise plan (25 points). ELR modernization approach (20 points). Budget justification and 2 CFR 200 compliance narrative (10 points).
generated_draft.submission_instructions: Deadline: May 28, 2021, 5:00 PM Eastern Time. Submit via Public Health Labs Grants Portal. Required: Narrative (20 pages), SF-424 Application, Budget Narrative, current emergency operations plan laboratory section, LRN membership documentation, most recent PHEP performance measure baseline data.

evaluator_notes: Perfect compliance score — explicitly references 2 CFR Part 200, 45 CFR Part 46, SF-425, and no-supplanting requirement. All 8 sections fully populated. Parameters exact match. PHEP program framing accurate: OPHPR/DSLR, LRN-B, All-Hazards, 24/7 activation benchmarks. Exercise requirements (2/year, tabletop + functional) correctly specified. Groundedness very high — all claims traceable to PHEP cooperative agreement program requirements.
